metadata.title: A two-tail obstruction to ambient conjugation in Dlab groups
metadata.description:
We give an affirmative answer to the corrected Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.149. The compact-support Dlab group with slopes in the powers of two has an order automorphism that cannot be implemented by conjugation after any embedding into any standard real Dlab group. The ambient slope group is unrestricted, the embedding need not preserve an order, and the conclusion includes the full and reflected extended-real families.

The proof uses perfectness to separate the supports of commuting local groups, least action components and finite-tuple transitivity to obtain one uniform orientation, and a normalizer with infinitely many bump components near both source endpoints. One of these tails forces a forbidden descending sequence of ambient support components. A solvable affine-germ quotient treats the real-line left endpoint. The paper credits Gong, Yang and Zeng, arXiv:2609.18630, for the prior six-family rank-one theorem and one-tail support obstruction. It also distinguishes the earlier formally verified non-inner formulation from the corrected ambient question.

The six-page note is accompanied by LaTeX source, an exact-rational construction verifier, source and priority audits, and independent AI adversarial-review records. Finite checks supplement the theoretical proof and do not certify universal claims about embeddings. Literature searches through 17 October 2026 found no earlier result with the unrestricted quantifiers; this is a bounded priority assessment. AI tools were used extensively in discovery, development, writing and verification. The preprint has not undergone independent human peer review, and no formal proof-assistant verification of this new theorem is claimed. Paper, prose and code: CC BY 4.0.

whole_config_original.title: A two-tail obstruction to ambient conjugation in Dlab groups
whole_config_original.description: An order automorphism of a Dlab group resists ambient conjugation after every embedding, with unrestricted slopes and precise endpoint conditions.
whole_config_original.abstract: Let $G=D_{\langle2\rangle}([0,1])$ be the compactly supported, locally right $2^{\mathbb Z}$-affine Dlab group. We construct an automorphism preserving both Dlab orders and give a proof that it cannot be implemented after any embedding in either of two explicitly defined groups: all locally right affine increasing interval homeomorphisms, and all locally right affine increasing real homeomorphisms that are affine on an initial ray. The ambient slopes are unrestricted, and the embedding need not preserve an order. Perfectness separates the supports of commuting local groups; a two-tail construction handles both possible orientations of their least action components. This extends a one-tail mechanism used in prior work. The definitions and affine-germ decomposition of the standard Dlab families place them in these ambient groups. Consequently the construction gives an affirmative answer to the corrected Kourovka Problem 21.149, including arbitrary positive-real slope groups and the full and reflected extended-real families.
plain_language: An automorphism changes the elements of a group while preserving how they compose. Conjugation implements such a change by moving to new coordinates: the same coordinate change is applied before and after every group element. An automorphism can fail to be conjugation inside its own group yet become conjugation in a larger group.

This paper constructs an automorphism of a Dlab group for which that larger-group route also fails in the stated ambient groups. The conclusion holds after every abstract injective embedding, including embeddings that do not preserve an order. The slopes allowed in the ambient group can be any positive real numbers.

The construction uses infinitely many small affine bumps approaching both ends of the source interval. A faithful action can arrange the relevant local regions in either of two orientations. One of the two tails then forces a proposed conjugating map to have a descending sequence of support components, which the ambient endpoint conditions forbid.
result: All maps are increasing, and group multiplication is ordinary composition. A map is **locally right affine** when, at every finite point $a$ other than a right endpoint, there are $\epsilon>0$ and $s>0$ such that
$$f(x)=f(a)+s(x-a)\qquad(a\le x\le a+\epsilon).$$

Let $\mathcal A_I$ be the group of these homeomorphisms of $[0,1]$, **including a right affine germ at $0$**. Let $\mathcal A_{\mathbb R}$ be the group of these homeomorphisms of $\mathbb R$ that also agree with $x\mapsto sx+t$, for some $s>0$, on an **initial ray at $-\infty$**. Positive ambient slopes are unrestricted. Infinitely many affine pieces and accumulation of pieces from the left are permitted.
The source group is
$$G=D_{\langle2\rangle}([0,1])=\{f\in\mathcal A_I:\text{ every right slope lies in }2^{\mathbb Z},\ f=\mathrm{id}\text{ near }0\text{ and }1\}.$$

**Theorem 2.** There is one automorphism $\alpha$ of $G$ preserving both Dlab bi-orders such that, for either $A=\mathcal A_I$ or $A=\mathcal A_{\mathbb R}$, every injective homomorphism $e:G\to A$ and every $u\in A$ satisfy
$$e(\alpha(f))\ne u^{-1}e(f)u\qquad\text{for some }f\in G.$$

The same automorphism works for both ambients and every subgroup of either ambient. The embedding is arbitrary as an abstract group embedding; no order on the ambient or order preservation by the embedding is assumed.

**Corollary 8.** Equip $G$ with either Dlab order. For any multiplicative subgroup $H\le\mathbb R_{>0}$, the automorphism cannot be implemented by conjugation after any embedding into any of the eight standard real Dlab families
$$D_H(I),\quad D_{H*}(I),\quad D_{*H}(I),\quad\overline D_H(I),\qquad D_H,\quad D_{H*},\quad D_{*H},\quad\overline D_H.$$

This includes the full and reflected extended-real families and gives an affirmative answer to the corrected ambient-conjugation formulation of Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.149. The standard real-line families retain their defining initial affine behavior at $-\infty$; a rank-one restriction on $H$ is not imposed.
### Why the initial affine ray matters

**Proposition 7.** Let $\mathcal B$ consist of all increasing real homeomorphisms that are locally right $2^{\mathbb Z}$-affine at every finite point and have support bounded above, with **no condition at $-\infty$**. For every automorphism $\beta$ of $G$, there are an embedding $E:G\to\mathcal B$ and $v\in\mathcal B$ such that
$$E(\beta(f))=v^{-1}E(f)v\qquad\text{for every }f\in G.$$
The countermodel is explicit. For $n\in\mathbb Z$, take $I_n=(-2^{-n},-2^{-n-1})$ and the increasing affine bijection $\phi_n:[0,1]\to\overline{I_n}$. Define
$$E(f)|_{I_n}=\phi_n\beta^n(f)\phi_n^{-1},\qquad v(x)=\begin{cases}x/2,&x<0,\\x,&x\ge0.\end{cases}$$

The maps $E(f)$ fix every cell endpoint and are the identity on $[0,\infty)$. The relation $v\phi_n=\phi_{n+1}$ gives the displayed conjugation identity. For nonidentity $f$, its copies act nontrivially in every cell while fixing cell endpoints arbitrarily far left, so $E(f)$ is not eventually affine on an initial ray. Thus $\mathcal B$ is a genuine boundary of the theorem and is not identified with the standard reflected Dlab family.
why_it_works: Dlab's classical algebraic simplicity theorem makes the source group and its interval copies perfect. The affine-germ centralizer argument then separates the action supports of commuting local groups. Simplicity supplies faithful local actions, and exact finite-tuple interpolation gives a single global orientation for their least action components.

A homeomorphism $h$ with bumps approaching both source endpoints defines $\alpha(f)=h^{-1}fh$. Its interior slopes are powers of two, and conjugation preserves each first nontrivial right slope, hence both Dlab orders. The map $h$ itself has no right affine germ at $0$ and is not in $\mathcal A_I$.

Any proposed ambient implementation must act nontrivially in every selected local region. Depending on the global orientation, the left or right source tail forces its support components to descend indefinitely. Right affine germs and the initial real affine ray rule out that behavior. The proof uses classical simplicity, order and affine-germ machinery; the finite rational construction checks supplement the mathematical proof.
limitations: The right germ at $0$ in $\mathcal A_I$ and eventual affine formula at $-\infty$ in $\mathcal A_{\mathbb R}$ are essential hypotheses. The theorem concerns these explicit ambient groups and their subgroups. It does not assert an obstruction in every homeomorphism group; Proposition 7 supplies the precise larger-group countermodel.

The defining maps are locally affine from the right, with arbitrary real breakpoints. They need not have finitely many pieces on a compact interval. Fixed initial neighborhoods arising from perfectness may depend on the element; a common fixed neighborhood for a whole perfect subgroup is not assumed.

The contribution concerns the unrestricted ambient slopes, arbitrary embeddings, and the full eight-family conclusion. Historical first priority remains unestablished. No claim about the present open status of related questions is made.

whole_config_original.description: Low-degree restrictions and an exact order-seven invariant for ordinary rational string-link invariants on actual free exteriors.
whole_config_original.abstract: We give applications of published finite-type classification and classical genus-two symmetry to the locus of string links with free exterior group. The category is ordinary unframed smooth ordered string links with fixed boundary, upward orientation, and rational invariants. Freeness means that the actual three-dimensional exterior group is abstractly F_k. Recalling a filtered Habegger–Masbaum corollary, the intersection of the entire Milnor algebra with the two-strand order-at-most-two space is span_ℚ{1, ℓ, ℓ²}. Meilhan's classification and known free tangles give a component Conway coefficient outside the Milnor-plus-vanishing span at (k,n)=(2,2), and give zero vanishing kernel for every k ≥ 2 and 0 ≤ n ≤ 2. An exact marked genus-two reversal argument, combined with the prior Duzhin–Karev ordinary orientation detector, gives a nonzero kernel invariant of exact order seven on two strands. The seven-wheel is credited to Bar-Natan following Duzhin–Karev's journal proof. Historical priority of these combined free-exterior applications is undetermined; no firstness is claimed.
plain_language: A string link is a collection of knotted strands in a cylinder, with labelled endpoints held fixed. Finite-type invariants are numerical probes of how those strands are knotted and linked.

This note studies the links whose surrounding three-dimensional exterior has a free fundamental group. That simple group condition still allows information beyond the linking number: a component Conway coefficient cannot be recovered by combining the relevant Milnor invariants with invariants that vanish on this whole locus.

Through order two, an ordinary rational invariant that vanishes on every such free exterior must be the zero invariant. On two strands, an existential order-seven invariant behaves differently: it is nonzero as an invariant but vanishes on every free exterior.
definitions: The category is smooth, ordered and labelled string links with fixed boundary and standard endpoint collars. Strands are oriented from bottom to top; upward orientation does not require height monotonicity. No strand framing is specified. Invariants are ℚ-valued and ordinary finite type, using both self-crossings and mixed crossings.

Let 𝓥ₙ(k) be the space of invariants of order at most n, including constants, and let 𝓕ₖ consist of links whose actual three-dimensional exterior group is abstractly the free group F_k. No preferred-meridian-basis condition is imposed. Define 𝓝ₙ(k) = {v ∈ 𝓥ₙ(k) : v(L) = 0 for every L ∈ 𝓕ₖ}.

Let 𝓜ₙ(k) = 𝓥ₙ(k) ∩ ℚ[μ_I : I any multi-index]. This is the intersection with the entire algebra of finite polynomials in based Milnor invariants, allowing repeated indices, arbitrary lengths and cancellations in a polynomial presentation.
result: For two strands, with ℓ = μ₁₂ = linking number, the recalled filtered Habegger–Masbaum corollary gives 𝓜₂(2) = span_ℚ{1, ℓ, ℓ²}. If a₁ is the Conway z² coefficient of the first individually closed strand, then a₁ ∉ 𝓜₂(2) + 𝓝₂(2). Thus the universal affirmative spanning assertion fails at (k,n) = (2,2).
For every k ≥ 2 and every 0 ≤ n ≤ 2, 𝓝ₙ(k) = 0.
There exists a nonzero rational invariant in 𝓝₇(2) of exact ordinary order seven. Consequently 𝓝ₙ(2) ≠ 0 for every n ≥ 7; the same invariant supplies these inclusions.
why_it_works: Published classification results describe all order-at-most-two invariants. Known free tangles, pure braids and disk-separated insertions isolate their coefficients, while filtered concordance results control the entire Milnor-algebra intersection.

For two free-exterior strands, the exterior is a genus-two handlebody. Classical hyperelliptic symmetry, with the full boundary marking and collars respected, supplies simultaneous strand reversal. Antisymmetrizing the prior ordinary Duzhin–Karev orientation detector then gives the order-seven vanishing invariant.
limitations: The order-seven invariant is existential and noncanonical. The note does not supply a canonical evaluator or a nonzero value on a named nonsingular string link; its diagram-weight calculation is not such a link evaluation.

The result does not determine orders three through six, the least positive kernel order, higher-strand higher-order kernels, or a general higher-order spanning classification. Failure of spanning at order two alone does not establish failure at larger order bounds.

Only disk-separated insertion is used for the free-locus construction. Arbitrary stacking or deletion of strands is not asserted to preserve the free-exterior condition. The theorem remains in the stated ordinary, unframed, smooth, rational category.

Historical priority of the combined free-exterior applications is undetermined. The older Morimoto and Li free-tangle papers remain unresolved priority comparisons. No worldwide firstness or current worldwide openness is claimed.
background: The questions come from Stanford’s Question 2.13 in Ohtsuki’s Problems on invariants of knots and 3-manifolds. The note gives the three stated restricted applications rather than a general classification.

Habegger–Masbaum supply the filtered Milnor/concordance input, with Casson’s concordance attribution through the inspected primary interfaces. Meilhan supplies the complete ordinary order-two classification, and Meilhan–Yasuhara give the relevant Milnor-invariant context.

Nogueira’s known free tangles and Kauffman–Lambropoulou’s rational-tangle geometry supply the geometric examples. The torus-knot Conway coefficients are credited to Alvarez–Labastida through Willerton.

The genus-two argument uses classical Bleiler–Moriah context, Rubinstein–Scharlemann and Bruno–Mecchia symmetry, and Hatcher’s relative-ball theorem. Duzhin–Karev supply the prior ordinary orientation detector; the seven-wheel is credited to Bar-Natan following their journal proof.

metadata.description:
This unrefereed, extensively AI-assisted application note studies ordinary unframed smooth ordered string links with fixed boundary and upward orientation; upward does not impose height monotonicity. Invariants are rational and freeness concerns the actual three-dimensional exterior group, abstractly the free group of rank k, without a primitive-meridian condition.

The entire all-length repeated-index Milnor algebra intersected with the two-strand order-at-most-two space is recalled as the span of 1, linking, and linking squared, a filtered Habegger–Masbaum corollary. Applications of Meilhan's complete classification and prior free tangles show that a component Conway coefficient is outside the Milnor-plus-vanishing span at (k,n)=(2,2), and that the vanishing kernel is zero for all k≥2 and 0≤n≤2. Exact marked genus-two reversal, combined with the prior Duzhin–Karev ordinary detector, gives an existential nonzero kernel invariant of exact ordinary order seven on two strands, hence nonzero kernels for every n≥7.

The wheel is credited to Bar-Natan following Duzhin–Karev's journal proof. Known tangle examples, rational 3/2 geometry, classical genus-two machinery, and Hatcher's relative-ball theorem are credited in the manuscript. Historical priority of the combined applications is undetermined; no firstness or new detector is claimed. Orders three through six, least positive kernel order, and higher-order classification are unaddressed by this work. Morimoto (1995) and Li (2009) remain unread priority leads and are not mathematical dependencies.

AI was used extensively in solving, verification, source investigation, and writing. Internal AI audits are not conventional human peer review or formal certification. New finite arithmetic programs in the supporting kit provide supplementary stage evidence, not full theorem proof; the unchanged original edition is theoretical and delivered no executable replay. No numeric value of the existential invariant on a named nonsingular link is supplied.
